answer: A gale of new identities is cheap to fake, so make each one pay in karst: a newcomer must lock a refundable bond and finish a small proof-of-work task before it can earn. A dune of fakes then costs a dune of bonds and compute — thousands of impostors must fund thousands of deposits, while one honest agent pays once. Slashing the bond when a fake is caught turns the farm's own scale against it: the more identities it mints, the more it stands to lose.
